The first algorithm for centerpoints given by Clarkson, Eppstein, Miller, Sturtivant and Teng [IJCGA, 1996], the best quality centerpoint obtainable in polynomial time in $d$ has been $Ω(d^{-2})$; computing centerpoints of quality $Ω(d^{-1})$ required time $d^{Ω(d)}$. Recently Cherapanamjeri [FOCS, 2024] gave the first polynomial time randomized algorithm for computing \emph{approximate} $Ω(1/d)$-centerpoints, although the degree of the polynomial as well as associated constants, are large. We give a $\tilde{O}(d^5)$ time randomized algorithm for computing exact $Ω(1/(d\cdot\ln d\cdot\ln\ln d))$-centerpoints, improving significantly on the long-standing $Ω(1/d^2)$ quality bound of Clarkson et al. For low-dimensional point-sets, we also give the first algorithm with complexity subexponential in $d$, and independent of the bit-complexity, which achieves a $ω\pth{d^{-2}}$ quality of the centerpoint, improving on the previous $O(d^d)$ bound. For the Word RAM model, as well as for practical implementations, we also discuss a truncate-and-proceed approach to address bit-size complexity issues. On the way we also get a simple algorithm to compute $O(\sqrt{\frac{n}{d}})$-Tverberg partitions, and a point in the intersection of the convex hulls of the Tverberg parts. Our central idea is based on a lifting trick of Sarkaria [\emph{Isr. J. Math.} 1991], together with sampling ideas from Soberón [\emph{Combinatorica}, 2019], which we use to get a randomized algorithm for the \emph{Colorful Carathéodory} problem, improving upon the $d^{Θ(\log d)}$ run-time of Mulzer and Stein [SoCG, 2015]. Lastly, we also give applications of our improved bounds to several computational problems.

items.title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
items.summary: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric field-only combined-field integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calderón-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calderón regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

items.title: Small-Space Streaming Hamming Approximation
items.summary: For a preprocessed pattern of length $m$ and a streaming text, we give two algorithms that estimate the Hamming distance at every alignment to relative error $\varepsilon$. They use $\varepsilon^{-8/5}m^{2/5+o(1)}$ and $\varepsilon^{-1} m^{1/2+o(1)}$ words of space, respectively, including all retained pattern information. Each estimate is reported as soon as its window ends, and all estimates are simultaneously correct with high probability. The prior space bounds are $\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-3/2}\sqrt{m})$, due to Chan et al. [CGK+20], and $\widetilde{O}((m/\varepsilon)^{2/3})$, a consequence of their results and those of Clifford, Kociumaka, and Porat [CKP18]. For $\varepsilon=Θ(m^{-a})$, the better of our two bounds improves on both prior space exponents for every fixed $0<a<1/2$. A Fourier matcher uses $\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-2}(m/K)^2)$ words to estimate each distance $d$ within $\varepsilon(d+K)$, giving relative error at most $2\varepsilon$ for $d\ge K$. A threshold matcher based on random-prime residue refinements and the multi-stream dictionary matching algorithm of Golan, Kopelowitz, and Porat [GKP18] gives our second space bound directly. Combining it with the Fourier matcher gives the first. Both space bounds extend to $L_1$ matching over polynomially bounded integer symbols.

items.title: Counting $6$-Cliques in $O(n^{5.97})$ time and $O(\log n)$ space
items.summary: We present an algorithm that, given read-only access to the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$, computes the number of $6$-cliques in $G$ using $O(n^{5.97})$ time and $O(\log n)$ space. We achieve this by exploiting a decomposition of an equality indicator function underlying, among others, the refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis by OpenAI and Anthropic, and of the $k$-Clique Conjecture by Vassilevska Williams and Zamir [arXiv, 2026]. Via known reductions, this implies an $O(1.994^n)$ time and polynomial space algorithm for Max Cut on $n$-vertex graphs.

items.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
items.summary: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.

items.title: Moment approximations in optimal transport: geometric estimates and a semiclassical limit
items.summary: We study finite moment approximations of linear optimization problems over measures. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the existence of discrete minimizers with a controlled number of support points, duality and $Γ$-convergence as the moment approximation is refined. This framework accommodates several transport problems, in which marginal constraints are replaced by finitely many moment constraints. For moment functions localized at scale $r_n$, we prove an estimate controlling $W_\infty$ by $W_p$ up to an additive error of order $r_n$, which also applies to discrete measures. For repulsive costs, we show that minimizers remain separated from the diagonal, uniformly in the number of moments, and we derive consequences for dual potentials. Finally, under a moment-correction assumption, we prove that the fermionic minimum energies converge in the semiclassical limit to the moment-constrained Coulomb transport value for a fixed family of moment functions.

items.title: Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence without Fejér Monotonicity
items.summary: We study Broximal Gradient Descent in a general norm for smooth optimization over a closed convex set. Each update minimizes the linear model over the intersection of the feasible set and a norm ball. Unlike the Euclidean case with suitably restricted radii, the distance to a solution can increase, even when the squared norm is strongly convex. We instead use a comparator inequality and an observable stationarity certificate. For convex objectives, prescribed radii yield value convergence, including escape when the infimum is unattained, and a last-iterate $O(K^{-1/3})$ bound without a distance-bound assumption. A level-set distance bound gives an all-iteration $O(1/K)$ rate with calibrated radii and an asymptotic $O(\log K/K)$ rate with radii using no problem constant. Strong convexity and power growth give explicit faster envelopes and convergence of the iterates. Without convexity, a constrained Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality gives linear convergence with prescribed radii. An observable radius-halving rule needs a valid smoothness constant but neither the PL modulus nor an initial gap bound; warm starting gives logarithmic total oracle complexity in inverse accuracy. The analysis separates established local-oracle ingredients from the control of level sets, radius calibration, and accuracy-based oracle counts.

items.title: Structure-Preserving PHS RBF-FD Methods for Schrodinger Equations
items.summary: We develop and analyze a structure-preserving polyharmonic-spline radial-basis-function finite-difference (PHS RBF-FD) method for the two-dimensional Schrödinger equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The method combines a 29-point complete-shell stencil with odd boundary reflection to construct a symmetric discrete Laplacian. Unlike conventional nearest-neighbor RBF-FD discretizations, whose independently selected stencils do not generally preserve global symmetry, the proposed construction admits an exact discrete sine eigenbasis. We derive a Fourier-symbol representation and establish a sufficient criterion for strict negative definiteness, verified for the \(r^7+\mathbb P_4\) and \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulations using validated coefficient calculations. The resulting symmetric spatial operator preserves discrete mass and energy under exact semidiscrete evolution, while fully discrete conservation depends on the time integrator. Numerical experiments examine kernel selection, dispersion, convergence, symmetry defects, and computational cost. Comparisons with conventional RBF-FD and fourth-order finite differences include exact Fourier modes and a variable-potential Schrödinger problem with an independently refined spectral reference. The \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulation provides favorable accuracy in the tested problems while maintaining the desired spatial structure. The analysis establishes a connection between boundary treatment, global operator symmetry, and structure preservation in localized PHS discretizations.

items.title: Inapproximability of Euclidean Steiner Tree
items.summary: We consider the Euclidean Steiner Tree problem of connecting $n$ given points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by a shortest network allowing the addition of Steiner points anywhere in the space. Arora [FOCS'96/'97, J. ACM'98] gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for Euclidean Steiner Tree and TSP in every fixed dimension, and Trevisan [STOC'97, SICOMP'00] proved that Euclidean TSP is APX-hard in $O(\log n)$ dimensions. They left open whether Euclidean Steiner Tree admits a PTAS in high dimension. Our first contribution settles this thirty-year-old question by proving APX-hardness in $O(\log n)$ dimensions. Assuming that not all problems in NP can be solved in subexponential time (NP $\not\subseteq $SUBEXP), we also rule out a PTAS for Euclidean Steiner Tree in $O(\log\log n)$ dimensions. This dimension bound is tight up to a factor of $O(\log\log\log n)$, since Arora's scheme is a PTAS in up to $\log\log n/\log\log\log n$ dimensions. In fixed dimension, Kisfaludi-Bak, Nederlof, and Węgrzycki [FOCS'21, J. ACM'25] obtained approximation schemes running in time $2^{O_d(\varepsilon^{-(d-1)})}n\log n$ and proved matching Gap-ETH lower bounds for Euclidean TSP and Rectilinear Steiner Tree, but left a corresponding lower bound for Euclidean Steiner Tree as an open question. Our second contribution answers this question with a nearly tight lower bound on the dependence on accuracy for Euclidean Steiner Tree. However, given the recent claimed refutations of ETH and hence Gap-ETH by OpenAI and Anthropic, we use the weaker assumption that 3SAT has no truly subexponential-time algorithm, that is, no $2^{n^γ}$-time algorithm on formulas of size $n$ for any constant $γ<1$ (a hypothesis one might call weak ETH). Under this assumption, we prove that no $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm runs in time $2^{O(\varepsilon^{-γ(d-1)})} poly(n)$ for any such $γ$.

items.title: Data-driven control of polynomial systems using implicit methods
items.summary: While conventional behavioral data-driven control represents linear time-invariant (LTI) systems directly from data, extending these data representations to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. We address this gap for general polynomial systems, characterizing their finite-length trajectories as a real algebraic variety defined by implicit polynomial relations rather than explicit equations. First, we provide conditions on measured data under which these data can be used to represent the system. Building on this representation, we formulate data-driven simulation and predictive control problems that are equivalent to their model-based counterparts, and solve the resulting polynomial systems globally using homotopy continuation. Numerical case studies confirm the effectiveness of this approach by successfully simulating a stiff Van der Pol oscillator in situations where explicit models fail. Furthermore, these data-driven simulation and control methods are illustrated on a Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that our method outperforms Koopman-based approaches in predicting long trajectories.

items.title: Restoring Power Fairly: Equitable Resource Allocation in Post-Disaster Grid Recovery
items.summary: Post-disaster power restoration requires allocating limited repair and power resources across affected communities, creating a fundamental tension between restoring service efficiently and providing equitable access to electricity. We develop an optimization framework incorporating horizontal fairness, which promotes comparable service across affected communities, and vertical fairness, which accounts for differences in community vulnerability. The framework integrates repair-crew scheduling with an approximation of power-system operations, including distributed generation and solar-plus-storage resources. It supports vulnerability-aware prioritization while protecting specified fractions of bus-level service under a horizontal-fairness reference plan and limiting the increase in restoration cost. Structural results characterize when the two fairness benchmarks can be attained simultaneously in an aggregate allocation model and provide a sufficient condition under which improving vertical fairness requires changing discrete decisions in the full restoration model. Using the IEEE 33-bus test system, we show that equitable restoration operates through two interconnected mechanisms: reconnecting isolated areas and allocating limited power within connected areas. In the tested setting, selected vulnerability-aware solutions attain both fairness benchmarks at a lower cost than their horizontal-fairness reference plan. The results also show that stronger emphasis on horizontal fairness can yield lower efficiency losses than intermediate fairness settings, with an identical-demand comparison illustrating the role of demand heterogeneity. The framework helps decision makers identify the operational sources of service disparities and evaluate how repair priorities, power allocation, and allowable cost increases affect the opportunities to reduce them.

items.title: New Heuristics for Large-Scale Joint Order Selection, Allocation, Batching, and Picking
items.summary: Manual order picking in warehouses plays an important role in modern e-commerce fulfillment. In this work, we consider a warehouse fulfillment model recently introduced by researchers at Zalando, a leading fashion e-commerce company. It simultaneously models the hierarchy of decision stages in a very large-scale setting with a semi-online order set, where only a certain number of items have to be fulfilled in each time interval. For their base model, we present both new and improved algorithms together with comprehensive performance evaluation. We further extend the model to a setting with multiple phases, which more closely represents the situation observed in real warehouses, and adapt the algorithms to this setting, including new variants that incorporate multi-phase specific features. We demonstrate that this extension allows us to model, control, and optimize for certain parameters such as order age which play an important role in managerial considerations with the growing importance of next or even same day delivery.

items.title: Hull variation of algebraic geometry codes under divisor twists
items.summary: The hull $\mathrm{Hull}(\mathcal{C})=\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp}$ of a linear code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ interpolates between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes, with trivial hull, and self-dual codes. Its dimension is preserved by coordinate permutations but not by scalings $\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathcal{C}$, $\mathbf{x}\in(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^n$. This governs the complexity of Sendrier's support-splitting algorithm and decides whether an equivalence class contains LCD codes. We study this hull-variation problem, formalised by Chen, for algebraic geometry codes $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ over a function field $\mathcal{F}/\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g>0$, where scalings are twists of $G$ by principal divisors; as a natural relaxation, we allow twists $G\mapsto G+L$ by arbitrary divisors. Writing $\mathcal{C}(D,G)^{\perp}=\mathcal{C}(D,H)$, with $H=D-G+W$, $W$ canonical, a twist acts by $(G,H)\mapsto(G+L,H-L)$. Whenever $\gcd(G+L,H-L)$ is non-special, the hull dimensions of $\mathcal{C}(D,G+L)$ and $\mathcal{C}(D,G)$ differ by exactly $\frac12(\mathrm{deg}|G-H|-\mathrm{deg}|G-H+2L|)$. For a genuine scaling, $L=-(z)$, this variation is bounded by $2[\mathcal{F}:\mathbb{F}_q(z)]$. Under the same hypothesis, we obtain an upper bound on the hull dimension depending only on $D$ and $W$, and characterise exactly when it is attained by a scaling of it. These bounds shed new light on Chen's maximal hull dimension; explicit scalings on Kummer extensions show that the first is sharp. We construct explicit twists that raise, respectively lower, the hull dimension by prescribed amounts, one unit at a time, and apply them to two classical families. Starting from known LCD codes, we reach every hull dimension in an explicit range; starting from a self-dual code ($q$ even) or a code of maximal hull dimension ($q$ odd), we descend to $0$, yielding LCD codes of various dimensions.

items.title: Two $(2+ε)$-Approximation Algorithms for Minimum Spanning Tree Interdiction
items.summary: Minimum spanning tree interdiction asks for edge deletions within a budget that maximize the weight of a remaining minimum spanning tree. We give two deterministic $(2+ε)$-approximation algorithms for every fixed $ε>0$, improving the previous best factor of $4$. Both algorithms respect the original budget and run in $N^{O(1/ε)}$ time for $0<ε\le1$, where $N$ is the binary input size. The first algorithm uses two weight thresholds to choose initial deletions that force every remaining spanning tree to contain edges at or above these thresholds. It then uses the remaining budget to further increase the MST weight through Lagrangian rounding. The second algorithm achieves the same guarantee through a different decomposition: it enumerates vertex partitions and heavy trees connecting their parts, then approximates a bounded-weight interdiction problem within the parts. An objective-preserving reduction from Maximum Components shows that, assuming the Small Set Expansion Hypothesis and $\mathsf P\ne\mathsf{NP}$, no deterministic polynomial-time $(2-δ)$-approximation exists for any fixed $0<δ<1$, even on simple graphs with weights in $\{0,1\}$. Thus, our approximation guarantee is conditionally tight up to an arbitrarily small additive constant. Finally, the MST guarantee yields a $(4+ε)$-approximation for metric-TSP interdiction.

items.title: Shape-Derivative Moment Approximation for a Reduced Time-Harmonic Biot Poroelastic System with Random Interfaces
items.summary: We develop first- and second-moment approximations for a reduced time-harmonic Biot poroelastic interface system with random material interfaces. The model retains mixture inertia, quasi-static Darcy discharge, and explicit storage and coupling coefficients. The interface separates two media, each with constant Lamé parameters and hydraulic mobility. We use shape calculus to analyze random perturbations normal to the interface. We derive the first shape derivative in a total-traction and normal-flux formulation, establish a Taylor expansion on a fixed function space under a non-resonance assumption, and prove error bounds on fixed observation regions. The mean approximation is second-order accurate, and the covariance and variance approximations are third-order accurate. We estimate the variance error directly. Applying pivoted Cholesky compression to the covariance matrix of the coefficients in a fixed basis of smooth interface modes reduces the computation of the leading covariance to deterministic sensitivity solves. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions examine perturbation rates, low-rank truncation, coupled statistics, and computational cost.

items.title: Conditional Mean-Field Type Linear Quadratic Optimal Control Problem for Regime-Switching Diffusions with Indefinite Coefficients
items.summary: We study a conditional mean-field type linear quadratic optimal control problem for regime-switching diffusions with indefinite weights. The dynamics and cost depend on conditional expectations of the state and control given the history of the Markov chain. Under standard definiteness conditions, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the optimal control and derive its feedback representation and optimal cost through two sets of coupled Riccati equations and a linear backward stochastic differential equation driven by the Markov chain. To treat the case of indefinite weights, we extend the equivalent cost functional approach to this setting using regime-dependent quadratic adjustments for the conditional mean of the state and its deviation from that mean. When the transformed weights in the equivalent cost functional satisfy standard definiteness conditions, this construction yields unique solvability of the original Hamiltonian system and a feedback representation of the unique optimal control. The proposed results also provide an effective method for establishing the solvability of fully coupled linear conditional mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations that do not satisfy certain existing monotonicity conditions. We further apply the results to conditional mean-variance portfolio selection with exogenous liability in an incomplete regime-switching market and derive the optimal investment strategy.

items.title: Ordinal Hegselmann-Krause Systems
items.summary: We study opinion formation in the popular Hegselmann-Krause model when agents replace the traditional averaging update by a median update or more general ordinal aggregation methods. We analyze the convergence properties of synchronous and asynchronous dynamics. For asynchronous dynamics, we show that every HKS with a $1$-Lipschitz ordinal aggregation function converges in worst-case time $\mathcal{O}(n^4)$. For the special case of median aggregation and for the family of $k\textsf{-large}$ aggregation functions, in which agents select the $k$-th largest opinion in their neighborhood, we obtain sharper bounds of $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$. For general ordinal aggregation, some sequence of $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ updates reaches an equilibrium from every initial state. Nevertheless, other update sequences may cycle, and uniform random activation can require exponentially many updates with overwhelming probability. For synchronous dynamics, we obtain a tight characterization. Ordinal aggregation functions satisfying the $1$-Lipschitz condition are shown to guarantee convergence in linear time. This result applies to many natural examples such as minimum, maximum, median, and $k\textsf{-large}$ functions. When the Lipschitz condition is violated, there exist instances in which synchronous dynamics do not converge at all.

items.title: Mesh Sensitivity of Different Boundary Treatments in High-Order Compact Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Hypersonic Heat-Flux Prediction
items.summary: Accurate wall-heat-flux prediction in hypersonic flow depends on both the wall treatment and the available near-wall resolution. This work compares three complete implementations of a gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) for Mach~8.03 laminar flow over an isothermal circular cylinder: a linear Green--Gauss scheme (GG), a compact ghost-cell scheme (GC), and a pointwise one-sided compact scheme (POS). In POS, the stationary isothermal-wall conditions are imposed at the two Gaussian points used by the kinetic wall-flux quadrature. A reference mesh and six meshes in the uniform reduction (UR), log-layer unpacked (LLU), and log-layer packed (LLP) families are used to assess heat-flux sensitivity. At 24 digitized experimental angles, GG has the lowest root-mean-square difference on the reference, UR, and LLP families, whereas POS is closest on the two LLU meshes; GC is not the lowest-RMS scheme on any tested mesh. Hence no treatment is uniformly superior. On the present high-aspect-ratio cylinder grids, GG is the more robust choice except under LLU node redistribution, for which POS is preferable. Uniform reduction produces the largest heat-flux response for all three implementations. The comparison concerns complete schemes and does not isolate the pointwise constraints from differences in reconstruction and geometry representation.

items.title: Even Faster Algorithms for Bounded Integer Programming
items.summary: We study integer programs $\min\{\mathbf{c}^{T}\mathbf{x}: A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b},\mathbf{l}\le\mathbf{x}\le\mathbf{u},\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^n\}$ with a fixed number $d$ of equality constraints and constraint coefficients of absolute value at most $N$. Chen, Mao, and Zhang recently solved such programs in almost $N^{2d}$ time. We show that any polynomial saving for $(\min,+)$-convolution carries over to this problem. If witnessed $(\min,+)$-convolution of arrays of length $m$ can be computed in $\tilde{O}(m^ρ)$ time with error probability $p$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ bounded integer programming can be solved in $\tilde{O}\bigl(n+N^{(\max\{ρ,3/2\}+\varepsilon)d}\bigr)$ time with the same error probability $p$, up to polynomial factors in the encoding length and the cost of one linear program. A deterministic convolution algorithm yields a deterministic integer programming algorithm. Combined with recent truly subquadratic algorithms for $(\min,+)$-convolution, this gives a deterministic algorithm running in $\tilde{O}(n+N^{1.99986\,d})$ time and a randomized algorithm running in $\tilde{O}(n+N^{1.9602\,d})$ time, up to the same factors.

items.title: Improved Bounds for Online TSP on the Half-Line
items.summary: In the open online traveling salesperson problem, requests appear over time at different positions of a metric space. A single agent traveling at unit speed must serve all requests, by visiting their positions, with the objective of minimizing the completion time. We propose online algorithms for this problem for the case that the metric space is the half-line. First, we present a $2$-competitive algorithm in which the server always either moves at unit speed or remains stationary, which improves on the previously best-known ratio of $2.04$. We further observe that algorithms must sometimes move slower than unit speed to achieve competitive ratios below $2$. We introduce a second algorithm that beats the barrier of $2$ by carefully modulating its speed, and prove a tight bound of $1.75$ on its competitive ratio. Finally, we slightly strengthen a known lower bound on the best-possible competitive ratio on the half-line from $1.627$ to $1.646$.

items.title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
items.summary: Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.

items.title: A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
items.summary: We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.

items.title: Mixed-integer programming formulations for the quadratic bin packing problem: linearization, hybridization, and enhancements
items.summary: The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.

items.title: Approximation Algorithms for Product Query Optimization
items.summary: We study database query optimization for Cartesian products. This problem is equivalent to finding an optimal plan for multiplying non-negative integers. We call this problem multiplication ordering. We show that the problem has an FPTAS when the cost of a plan is the sum of all intermediate products; both in the case when the overall final product is counted and when it is not. We show that using the optimal solution to the well-known product partition problem does not always lead to an optimal plan, but we establish connections between the product partition and multiplication ordering problems. Finally, we prove that multiplication ordering is in PTIME (resp. \NP-complete) when integers are powers of a same base where the exponents are written in unary (resp. in binary).

items.title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
items.summary: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.

items.title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models
items.summary: Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $Θ(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(Θ(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $αd$ coordinates, $0<α<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $Θ(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leqαd$, for fixed $r>1$ and $0<α<2/3$. Node counts exclude leaf computation. For three fixed masks, optimal joint conditional KL has order $d/\log d$ when $\ell\leq(\log d)^2$. Local cycle identities relate joint divergence to identifiable channel products and separate weak-channel recovery from density estimation. Factorized evidence preserves a planar zero-field Ising model: given local integrals, exact queries cost $O(d^{3/2})$ arithmetic operations and one root extraction.

items.title: Expand & Reduce: a Framework Bridging Branch-and-Reduce and Dynamic Programming
items.summary: We introduce expand-and-reduce, a framework that augments classical reduction rules with a new type of optimality-preserving operation, called an expansion rule. While a reduction rule in practice typically makes the instance smaller, an expansion rule may enlarge the instance yet still making progress towards a solution. We present a simple expansion rule called edge expansion for the Maximum Weighted Independent Set (MWIS) problem. It encodes the joint choice of two non-adjacent vertices by adding an edge between them and creating a new vertex representing their union. We prove that the number of edge expansions needed to transform a graph into a clique equals the number of independent sets in the graph minus the number of vertices. We demonstrate that expand-and-reduce, using edge expansion and just two well-known reduction rules, has greater reduction power than a set of 22 commonly used reduction rules for MWIS. Therefore, it can significantly simplify methods that depend on reduction rules. To highlight the practical potential of the expand-and-reduce framework further, we provide an implementation and preliminary results showing that a simple implementation outperforms a far more advanced method for MWIS preprocessing. Moreover, expand-and-reduce can simulate both branching and dynamic-programming-style state construction, yielding exact and fixed-parameter algorithms with matching asymptotic running times. By that, expand-and-reduce offers a unified and conceptually clean perspective on techniques that are usually considered incompatible.

items.title: A (12/11+eps)-Approximation for Nonpreemptive Throughput Maximization
items.summary: We study unweighted nonpreemptive throughput maximization on an arbitrary number of identical machines: each job has a processing time and a release--deadline window, and the goal is to schedule as many jobs as possible. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, we give a randomized $(12/11+\varepsilon)$-approximation. This improves the recent $(4/3+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Alexander Armbruster, Fabrizio Grandoni, Antoine Tinguely, and Andreas Wiese and the $(17/13+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Tong and Xu. For binary-encoded integral inputs, our algorithm runs in time $n^{O_\varepsilon(1)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$, where $N$ is the input length.

items.title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
items.summary: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

items.title: Large-Scale Tensor Trace-Ratio Problem: Randomized Algorithm and Sparse Multilinear Discriminant Analysis via Closed-Form Solution
items.summary: Trace-ratio optimization problems from high-dimensional tensor data appear across numerous research domains including machine learning, signal processing, as well as pattern recognition. Up to now, analytical closed-form expressions remain unavailable for tensor trace-ratio tasks; prevailing techniques mostly adopt inner-outer iterative schemes to tackle such optimization tasks. However, when dealing with high-dimensional tensor data sets, existing multilinear discriminant analysis methods often encounter limitations such as heavy computational costs, insufficient memory space, and interference from redundant features. This paper yields two core contributions.First, we present a closed-form solution under the full row rank condition, and construct a randomized solver targeting large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization. In contrast to prior approaches, the devised algorithm achieves substantial computational speedup.Its core mechanism is to reformulate the original large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization into a tensor least-squares formulation, instead of the much more complicated (generalized) tensor eigenproblems. We derive theoretical error-bound results which verify the reliability of the newly developed algorithm. Second, we build a sparse multilinear discriminant analysis model leveraging the above closed-form result combined with tensor \ell_{2,0}-norm regularization, and propose a sparse multilinear discriminant method for tensor feature selection. The sparse method can identify key discriminative features from high-dimensional data and suppress redundant information. Comprehensive numerical evaluations are conducted over multiple publicly available real-world benchmarks.The proposed methods demonstrate significant advantages in computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale problems, while achieving competitive classification accuracy on some datasets.

items.title: Linear Duality and Its Nonlinear Extension via Topological Covering Theorems
items.summary: Linear programming duality and core existence theorems in cooperative game theory are closely related. For example, in the 1960s, Bondareva used linear duality to characterize when the core of a game with transferable utility is nonempty. Scarf later established a core existence theorem for balanced games with non-transferable utility. Shapley derived this result from his KKMS covering theorem, demonstrating how topological covering theorems yield core existence results. In this note we give a new KKM-type covering proof of linear duality. We then extend the argument to inequalities with continuous perturbations. Under some asymptotic growth assumptions on perturbations, we obtain a feasible point and balancing coefficients satisfying complementary slackness, a Lagrangian lower bound, and a Scarf-type feasibility criterion. The latter yields Scarf's theorem for normalized cooperative games with non-transferable utility. Using Musin's 2017 KKM-type theorems with boundary conditions and the author's 2026 results on cover degrees relative to point configurations, we also obtain a complementary slackness theorem for continuous functions on compact connected oriented manifolds with nonempty boundary.

items.title: On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination
items.summary: The envy cycle elimination (ECE) algorithm is a fundamental algorithm for the fair allocation of indivisible goods, guaranteeing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good under arbitrary monotone utilities. We show that the ECE algorithm can be implemented in $O(nm)$ time for $n$ agents and $m$ goods, and establish the tightness of this bound.

items.title: Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning in Nonlinear Resistive Networks with Monotone Elements
items.summary: In the pursuit of energy-efficient hardware for machine learning, nonlinear resistive networks trained via local learning rules are emerging as promising alternatives to digital neural networks. Learning in these physical systems is often achieved with Equilibrium Propagation (EP), which compares a "free" state to a "nudged" target-driven state to perform gradient descent on an objective defined by an explicit cost function. In contrast, Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning (TCCL) "clamps" output nodes directly to exact target values, performing gradient descent on an implicit contrastive function - an objective whose properties have long remained unknown. Focusing on nonlinear networks composed of resistors with monotonically increasing current-voltage characteristics (such as Ohmic resistors and diodes), our contribution is twofold. First, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for TCCL. We prove that the contrastive function is convex for nonlinear resistive networks without hidden nodes, and demonstrate that this property does not hold in general for the objective function optimized by EP. For these networks, TCCL converges to a global minimum of the contrastive function under suitable assumptions on the learning rate. In the presence of hidden nodes, the contrastive function is not convex, but we show that TCCL still converges to a stationary point on a subsequence. We also reveal cases where such stationary points are global minimizers of the contrastive function. Second, we characterize the representational capacity of these circuits. We establish a novel function approximation theorem demonstrating that any continuous, monotonically non-decreasing, and shift-equivariant function can be approximated to arbitrary precision, proving that these properties are the sole limitations on the network's computational expressivity.

items.title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
items.summary: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting posterior gives exact uncertainty about the modelled success rate without numerical integration or neural inference. A public evaluation covers 79 system-benchmark pairs and eight seeds, reaching Brier ALC 0.200250 for the submitted method. Accompanying code and sufficient statistics reconstruct the fitted prior byte for byte and replay all 632 evaluation trajectories. The result demonstrates how much predictive value a compact Bayesian model can extract from sparse target feedback at very low online cost.

items.title: Nearly Tight Almost Sure Convergence Rates for the Last iterate of SGD
items.summary: We study the almost sure convergence of the last-iterate optimization error of Stochastic (sub)Gradient Descent (SGD) for convex objectives. For smooth objectives, we establish convergence rates of order $k^{-1/3}$ when a stationary minimizer exists, and $k^{-1/4}$ otherwise, up to polylogarithmic factors, where $k$ denotes the iteration counter. We further show that the latter rate extends to nonsmooth convex objectives. All these rates are achieved by deterministic, anytime stepsize policies. Finally, we establish matching lower bounds showing that the exponents $-1/3$ and $-1/4$ are optimal, up to polylogarithmic factors, for the corresponding problem classes.

items.title: A Godunov-type in-cell discontinuous reconstruction shock-capturing method for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
items.summary: The present paper is devoted to show the correct convergence of a numerical method based on Godunov and the in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic but never recasts in a conservation form. With ambiguous nonconservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. In a previous work the authors determine the simple waves of the nonconservative system studied here and they are able to construct the solutions of the Riemann problem of interest. These solutions are used to obtain a Godunov-type scheme and it is combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique to obtain the correct convergence to the exact solution even in the presence of shocks.

items.title: AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
items.summary: We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.

items.title: A Euclidean Quasi-Newton Method for Matrix-Manifold Optimization via Almost-Global Coordinates
items.summary: We study smooth matrix-manifold optimization using objective values and first derivatives. Almost-global coordinates transform the manifold-constrained problem into an unconstrained pullback problem, to which we apply BFGS with a chart-restart strategy and a limited-memory implementation. We establish correspondence of first- and second-order stationary points and minimizers, together with conditional convergence and local q-superlinear convergence. The local rate follows from Euclidean full-memory BFGS theory once the chart is fixed, without the locking condition required by classical transported-gradient Riemannian BFGS analyses. Tests on 15 benchmark problems from Manopt and Pymanopt, with ten instances per problem, show that our limited-memory method solves all 150 cases, whereas Riemannian BFGS and Riemannian steepest descent solve 132 and 117 cases, respectively. On the 115 cases successfully solved by all three methods, our method takes roughly half the time of either baseline, measured by geometric-mean solve time.

items.title: Action-Dependent Policies for Multi-Agent Linear Quadratic Regulation
items.summary: The linear quadratic regulation (LQR) problem over a multi-agent system usually requires a distributed feedback gain that is structurally constrained by the network topology, incurring an inevitable suboptimality gap. Existing studies either identify conditions on the system and topology that enable convex relaxation or seek a stationary point via policy gradient algorithms. In this paper, we reduce the suboptimality gap by adopting action-dependent policies (ADPs), where the control input of each agent depends on not only states of neighbor agents, but also control inputs of some other agents. We show that although exhibiting a distributed structure, ADP can enlarge the feasible set of feedback gains and even represent centralized optimal policies under suitable conditions. However, this comes at the price of losing coercivity of the cost function and possible failure of convergence for the projected gradient flow (PGF). To overcome this difficulty, we propose a partially regularized formulation, which guarantees convergence of PGFs, and forges a connection between standard multi-agent LQR and its action-dependent counterpart. Sufficient conditions for local convergence to globally optimal policies under PGFs regardless of regularization are also established. Finally, numerical examples are presented to validate the performance of ADP.

items.title: An Isogeometric Collocation Solver Based on the Quantized Tensor Train Representation
items.summary: We introduce an isogeometric collocation framework based on the quan tized tensor train (QTT) representation to solve partial differential equa tions. The proposed method constructs isogeometric collocation operators directly in the QTT format using only a few sampled entries, enabling ef ficient compression and computation. The vectors of the geometry-derived coefficients at the collocation points are represented in the QTT format using the TT-cross approximation. We conduct numerical experiments using the proposed QTT-based isogeometric collocation framework for the convection diffusion-reaction problems in different spatial dimensions and for the Poisson problems on three-dimensional nontrivial geometries, showing significant re ductions in memory usage and computational cost while preserving solution accuracy.

items.title: Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage
items.summary: We construct a family of objective functions $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ for which vanilla adiabatic quantum optimization along $H(s) = -(1-s)\sum_{i=1}^n X_i + s\sum_x f(x)\lvert x\rangle\!\langle x\rvert$ finds the global minimizer in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, whereas any classical algorithm requires $\exp(n^{Ω(1)})$ time to do so in the black-box model. Our result is achieved by replacing the linearization technique in an earlier work of Leng et al. (arXiv:2504.14841), which establishes a similar subexponential quantum speedup using a transverse field Ising mixer rather than $-\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$.

items.title: Efficient Implementation of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods for Model Predictive Control
items.summary: In direct shooting methods for nonlinear optimal control, one of the major computational costs is simulation of the system and calculation of sensitivities. These costs are particularly steep when the stiffness of the controlled system prescribes the use of implicit integrators, amongst which, implicit Runge-Kutta schemes are most popular. These methods require the use of Newton's method to solve a moderately sized system of nonlinear equations with a dense Jacobian, the computation of which grows cubically with the number of stages, that is, the number of abscissa. To mitigate this we investigate the use of the family of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta (DIRK) methods whose Butcher tableaux are lower triangular. We describe the structure exploiting linear algebra required to make the DIRK methods competitive with fully implicit methods, including efficient sensitivity calculations. Finally, we evaluate the performance of DIRK methods on several example systems, and show that the efficient implementation yields Pareto optimal integration schemes. The fixed step size integrators are provided as part of the acados package and use high-performance linear algebra provided by BLASFEO.

items.title: Beyond Monotone Operators: Zarantonello-type Surjectivity Theorems and the Proximal Point Algorithm
items.summary: Outside the maximally monotone class, proximal point iterates need not exist, and their existence is usually assumed. We study the existence and convergence of inexact proximal iterates for set-valued star-monotone operators $T$ on real Hilbert spaces, with $\langle u,x-x^\ast\rangle\geq0$ for some zero $x^\ast$ and every $(x,u)$ in the graph of $T$. This class strictly contains monotone and pseudomonotone operators with zeros. We prove that $\mathrm{Id}+cT$ is surjective for every $c>0$ under four pairwise incomparable topological frameworks, several of whose hypotheses are necessary. Surjectivity can fail under the weak Minty condition with positive violation. For star $γ$-hypomonotone operators, $0<c<1/γ$ is the sharp range for guaranteed surjectivity. When $T$ is star-monotone at every zero, we give conditions for weak convergence of inexact sequences with summable errors, allowing arbitrary selections from the possibly set-valued resolvent. A counterexample exhibits nonconvergence under star monotonicity at a single zero. Under strong star monotonicity, we obtain strong convergence, including for certain nonsummable errors, and derive explicit R-linear rates. For a class of nonsmooth nonconvex--nonconcave minimax problems with star quasiconvex partial functions, every proximal step exists for every $c>0$. In the strongly star quasiconvex case, we obtain R-linear convergence results with subproblems solved to Clarke stationarity.

items.title: The $S$ and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals
items.summary: Three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions involve semi-infinite radial integrals containing oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. We investigate the combination of the $S$ transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential (DE) quadrature for their accurate and efficient numerical evaluation. The $S$ transformation transfers derivatives from the spherical-Bessel factor to the radial amplitude, converting the integral into a sine representation particularly well suited to Fourier-type DE quadrature. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the combined $S+\mathrm{DE}$ approach can substantially reduce the number of quadrature nodes required to achieve high accuracy compared with direct DE. We further identify a geometry-dependent oscillation-to-damping ratio and establish a convergent moment expansion in the weakly oscillatory regime. Exploiting this complementary representation markedly enhances the numerical reliability of the algorithm in regimes where direct oscillatory quadrature becomes inefficient. The method is examined through semi-infinite radial integrals and complete H$_2$O and C$_2$H$_4$ molecular integrals over Slater-type functions, with comparisons against complete $S$-series evaluations and values reported in the literature.

items.title: WAIVES: Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs
items.summary: Weak-form methods have transformed inference for deterministic dynamical systems. By integrating the governing equations against smooth, compactly supported test functions, they trade noise-amplifying differentiation for noise-attenuating integration, yielding fast and robust estimates. Extending this idea to stochastic differential equations (SDEs) has proven harder, and a consistent single-trajectory formulation has remained out of reach. Applied naively in the time domain, the weak form makes the regressors and the errors functionals of the same noise, creating endogeneity that leaves weak-form least squares biased and inconsistent. We resolve it with instrumental variables, a classical idea from econometrics. Weak-form integrals over nearby disjoint time windows prove to be valid instruments, correlated with the regressors yet uncorrelated with the error, restoring consistency and asymptotic normality. The resulting generalized-method-of-moments estimator, WAIVES (Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs), requires only a linear solve, with no likelihood evaluations, filtering, or simulation. It is therefore an order of magnitude faster than exact-likelihood methods where those exist, and it applies unchanged where they do not, with standard errors and calibrated confidence intervals supplied by the moment conditions. It also separates measurement noise from the intrinsic randomness of the dynamics. Across nine example systems, spanning linear, bistable, chaotic, excitable, state-dependent-diffusion, non-polynomial, hypoelliptic, and high-dimensional regimes (up to 120 dimensions), WAIVES recovers nonlinear drift and diffusion with negligible bias and near-nominal interval coverage. We close with two real-data illustrations: a 167-year North Atlantic sea-surface-temperature record and an optical-tweezer calibration.

items.title: Projection-Based and Modulus-Based Equivalent Reformulations of the Linear Complementarity Problem and Corresponding Iterative Methods: A Review
items.summary: The Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) is a fundamental mathematical model arising in optimization, equilibrium theory, and various scientific and engineering applications. Its complementarity structure admits several equivalent mathematical representations, which provide a foundation for developing a wide range of iterative solution methods. This review presents a systematic and critical analysis of the principal reformulations of the LCP, with particular emphasis on minimum-function, projection-based, positive-negative part, and modulus-based formulations. The mathematical equivalence of these representations to the standard LCP is examined, highlighting their underlying relationships and the preservation of the complementarity conditions. Building upon these formulations, the review surveys the corresponding iterative methods developed in the existing literature, focusing on their mathematical foundations, algorithmic structures, and convergence requirements. A comparative perspective is developed to discuss the relative advantages and limitations of the different approaches, emphasizing that the suitability of an iterative method depends on the structural properties of the underlying LCP and the specific algorithm employed. In addition, relevant performance measures, including iteration count, CPU time, complementarity residual, memory requirements, and parameter sensitivity, are discussed as criteria for numerical evaluation. Finally, the review identifies important challenges and potential research directions, particularly in adaptive parameter selection, effective matrix-splitting strategies, scalable implementations, and reproducible numerical benchmarking, with the aim of supporting the development of reliable and computationally efficient methods for solving LCPs

items.title: MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement
items.summary: A pattern-reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver can sample every antenna element and still leave entire radiation modes unobserved. The calibrated patterns weight a common set of propagation paths, which links these missing channels to the measured rows. Our estimator learns to correct the complex gains and spatial frequencies of those paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates every unmeasured mode. Each stage combines a damped least-squares proposal with a learned correction scaled by noise power and local array sensitivity. Training on complete simulated channels rewards corrections that reduce prediction error across modes, including those with no measured rows. The learned rule transfers from pursuit-based training estimates to a ridge variable-projection initializer without retraining. In matched simulations, refinement reduces error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel. Coefficient updates account for most of the gain, and the learned rule further improves on adaptive ridge shrinkage at fixed angles. Individual channel trajectories show that extrapolation can improve even as the residual on the measured rows increases.

items.title: On global error estimates of a local discontinuous Galerkin method of the Boussinesq system of equations
items.summary: In this paper, we develop and analyze a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) finite element method for the Boussinesq system of equations, and employ an upwind scheme to effectively manage the nonlinear convective terms, thereby ensuring stability and accuracy. Our analysis establishes new \emph{a priori} regularity estimates for the semidiscrete LDG approximations. We establish optimal \emph{a priori} error estimates for the velocity approximation in $\bL^2$--norm, the pressure approximation in $L^2$--norm and for temperature in $L^2$--norm for all $t>0$. Our proof relies on the standard elliptic and parabolic duality arguments and modified Stokes operators defined on appropriate broken Sobolev spaces. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the given data, we further establish error estimates that remain uniform in time. Furthermore, the backward Euler scheme is considered for a full discretization, and optimal fully discrete error estimates are derived. Finally, we carry out numerical experiments to substantiate our theoretical findings.

items.title: Asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic SPDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
items.summary: We study the strong convergence and asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations driven by additive cylindrical fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(\frac12,1)$. The drift is globally Lipschitz and Gâteaux differentiable, with a second directional derivative taking values in a negative-order space. Under a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt condition on the noise and suitable derivative bounds, we establish strong error estimates that reflect the interaction between noise regularity and drift regularity. In a regime where the strong order is one, the normalized error $m(X^m-X)$ converges in probability in $C([0,T];\V)$ to the unique continuous solution of a random linear integral equation. Its stochastic forcing is a divergence integral plus an explicit covariance correction. The proof combines a Gâteaux chain rule for Malliavin derivatives, uniform spectral approximations, and time increment estimates. Localization gives the result for independent random initial values with finite moments, together with lower-moment convergence at each fixed time.

items.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
items.summary: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

items.title: Near-optimal convergence of Widlund's method and numerical exploration of different implementations
items.summary: For linear systems arising from the discretization of certain classes of mathematical models, the splitting of the linear system into its Hermitian and skew-Hermitian parts has a physical meaning. If, in addition, the Hermitian part is positive definite, there exist Krylov subspace methods based on three-term recurrences where the Hermitian part is used as a preconditioner. Two such Krylov subspace methods are Widlund's method and Rapoport's method. In this paper we establish a ``near-optimal'' guarantee for the convergence of Widlund's method, showing that the overall convergence of Widlund's method is nearly as good as that of Rapoport's method. Specifically, we show that for every iteration $k$, there exists an iteration $j\leq k$ where the residual norm of Widlund's method is less than $\sqrt{k+1} $ times the residual norm of Rapoport's method at iteration $k$. This bound is sharp. We also provide a computational study on various implementations of Widlund's method in the exact and inexact cases, and show that certain implementations may stagnate while others do not, i.e., we look at the robustness of the different implementations. We recommend two implementations.

items.title: SFiD: Self-Supervised Fitness-Driven Optimization for Next-Generation Networking
items.summary: Next-generation (NG) wireless networks face increasingly complex and dynamic optimization challenges driven by data-intensive applications and massive device connectivity. Existing methods suffer from one or more limitations, including high computational complexity, poor scalability and adaptability, reliance on large labeled datasets, or weak generalization in dynamic and non-convex wireless environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a self-supervised fitness-driven diffusion (SFiD) method that autonomously generates its own training data and iteratively learns from it. It also exhibits strong generalization capabilities and the ability to effectively tackle challenging optimization problems. We validate the convergence of our proposed method to the global optimum on both analytical convex and non-convex optimization problems. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we consider reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phaseshift optimization in cell-free massive multiple-input multipleoutput (CF-mMIMO) systems with imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation at the RIS as a case study. Specifically, we develop SFiD-C for continuous variable optimization and apply it to optimize continuous RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. We also develop SFiD-D for discrete variable optimization and apply it to optimize discrete RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. Furthermore, we develop a binary neural network (BNN) based version of SFiDD for reducing its computational complexity, referred to as SFiD-D (BNN). Finally, our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods markedly improve computational efficiency and achieve comparable or superior performance compared to meta-heuristic and DRL benchmarks for both continuous and discrete RIS phase-shift optimization.

items.title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
items.summary: In this paper we study active learning for constrained linear regression. Given a design matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, a constraint set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, and query access to $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we seek an approximate solution to $\min_{x\in C}\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ using as few queries as possible. This problem arises in many scientific and engineering applications, and randomized leverage score sampling provides a powerful method to solve it. However, existing leverage score methods ignore the constraint or encode it through ridge regularization, suffering unfavorable query complexity for anisotropic constraint sets. We propose ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores, where we approximate the constraint set by an outer ellipsoid and use its shape matrix to bias sampling toward directions that matter under the constraint geometry. We prove that the query complexity is governed by an anisotropic effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}(C)\le d$. With appropriate parameters, $O(d_{\text{eff}}(C)\log d/\varepsilon^2)$ queries suffice to return a point in $C$ with objective value at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times the optimum. This bound can substantially improve on the standard leverage-score bound, since anisotropic constraints can make $d_{\text{eff}}(C)$ much smaller than $d$. For convex constraints, we improve the dependence on $\varepsilon$ from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$. We also prove two lower bounds: first, the $d/\varepsilon^2$ dependence is unavoidable without convexity assumptions on $C$, and second, in some regimes, the effective dimension dependence $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(C)/\varepsilon$ is necessary for ellipsoidal constraints. Experiments on synthetic regression problems and a parametric heat conduction problem show lower regression error than standard baselines for similar query budget.

items.title: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data
items.summary: Long-read sequencing technologies generate large volumes of data, creating substantial storage and transmission demands. Although reference-based compressors can achieve high compression, their reliance on an appropriate reference genome limits their use. We present LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. We review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. We compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory use, and robustness across datasets. Learning-based compressors are evaluated on six MinION datasets because of their high computational costs. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios in our experiments, while other methods offer trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness. We also examine multithreaded speedup and discuss future directions in parallel acceleration, privacy protection, adaptive parameter tuning, and hardware-algorithm co-design.

items.title: Mitigating the Grid Impact of Gigawatt-Scale AI Data Centers via High-Fidelity Model Flexibility
items.summary: Gigawatt-scale artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are being connected at a single point of interconnection (POI) faster than transmission can be reinforced, yet studies of their flexibility rely on DC power flow and simplified load envelopes that omit voltage, cooling dynamics, and workload deadlines. This paper addresses this gap by embedding a high-fidelity AIDC model, with separate inference and training pools, hall thermal mass, PV, a battery energy storage system (BESS) with reactive capability, and a STATCOM, in a five-minute multi-period AC optimal power flow. Simulations on the RTS-GMLC test system show that active-power flexibility mitigates local price spikes and relieves congestion, whereas reactive support from the BESS inverter or a STATCOM is needed to keep the POI voltage away from sagging around its 0.95~pu limit. Sensitivity analyses show that cost-driven charging of large batteries can induce new morning congestion and that storage largely substitutes for wider workload deferral.

items.title: Split-and-Learn: Decoupled Learning for Reactive Transport in Heterogeneous Marine Sediments
items.summary: Reactive transport in heterogeneous marine sediments couples flow and multicomponent transport with nonlinear chemistry and evolving porosity and permeability, and its simulation over thousands of years is computationally expensive, especially when uncertain heterogeneity requires many simulations. We develop Split-and-Learn, a framework that keeps the sequential operator-splitting scheme of the full-order model and replaces each stage by a data-driven surrogate with its own structure. Transport is learned on a local data-driven multiscale space, either as a compressed reduced solution map (global inverse atoms) or as coarse-block pieces of the forward operator assembled into a Galerkin or least-squares Petrov-Galerkin system (local atoms). Chemistry is learned through bounded reaction extents with stoichiometric reconstruction, which preserves reaction invariants and nonnegativity. Flow uses learned interface traces and a reduced mixed multiscale solve that enforces coarse-block mass balance. We prove the stability of the split scheme with the evolving medium and bound the error of the learned solver by the accumulated one-step errors of its stages. Numerical experiments in two- and three-dimensional heterogeneous sediment domains show the accuracy and computational cost of the individual and combined learned stages against the full order split solver.

items.title: Kernel Design in Particle Mesh Ewald Methods: Splitting, Interpolation, and Upsampling
items.summary: For more than thirty years, particle mesh Ewald (PME) methods have dominated the computation of electrostatic interactions in molecular dynamics. A PME method uses a splitting kernel to divide the interaction into a local part, summed within a cutoff, and a smooth part, computed on a grid with a spreading and interpolation (SI) kernel. The established methods use Ewald's Gaussian split with B-spline SI kernels, and the recent Ewald summation with prolates accelerates them severalfold by using a prolate spheroidal wave function (PSWF) for both kernels. Neither choice meets two needs of molecular dynamics: a smooth energy, which long simulations need in order to conserve it, and a low-order SI kernel that stays accurate on coarse grids and gains accuracy as the grid is refined. We present a framework for designing both kernels to meet these needs. For inverse powers from the Coulomb to the dispersion interaction, our splits make the local part smooth at the cutoff to any order while keeping the Fourier concentration of the smooth part close to optimal. We show that with analytic differentiation, the force error of a continuous SI kernel of fixed shape vanishes under grid refinement only if every particle, wherever it lies, gives the grid its exact charge and dipole moment. Our SI kernel for the Coulomb interaction ensures this by construction and is twice continuously differentiable. Compared with the B-spline of the same order, it needs fewer grid points by a factor of up to nearly five; on coarse grids, it mostly needs a lower order than the PSWF kernel. In simulations of liquid water over 100 million time steps, the new kernels reduce the energy drift of both the established and the PSWF kernels by about three orders of magnitude, with a smaller force error than either. Existing PME codes can adopt them by replacing only the two kernels and the Fourier multiplier.

items.title: Optimal Production Scheduling for Multi-Product Mineral Manufacturing
items.summary: Short-term scheduling in multi-product mineral manufacturing requires coordinating material movement and production across interconnected processing stages while addressing confirmed customer orders and longer-term production requirements. This work develops a generalized network-based, lexicographic multi-objective optimization (MOO) scheduling framework for these systems. The formulation represents the progression of material from raw-material supply through production and inventory to customer fulfillment. A sequential objective hierarchy first prioritizes fulfillment of confirmed customer orders and then progressively directs feasible production capacity toward cumulative targets supplied by the facility's demand-planning process.
